data.name: Copies, Not Thefts
data.description: Three of the Kage's letters were copied, not stolen. Get inside a private archive, take back the files, and bring home the ledger that names the buyer. How quietly you do it is up to you.
data.successDescription: Congratulations! You've successfully won the battle

objectives.description:
The briefing room is lit by one lantern over the map table. The Commander does not sit.

"Three of the Kage's letters left this village and came back as copies. Copies, not thefts. Someone wanted us blind, not angry.
The paper traces to a private archive that keeps records for anyone who pays."

nextObjectiveId.text: Who bought them?
Why is ANBU not handling this openly?

objectives.description:
She sets a marker on the map, well outside the wall.

"That is what you will find out. Bring back what they hold and the ledger that says who paid. Nobody knows you were there.
One detail, since you will be reading their shelves: that archive files by season, not by year. Anyone who asks for a year has never been inside."

nextObjectiveId.text: Understood.
And if the door is watched?

objectives.description:
The mission clerk has your kit ready before you reach the counter.

"Lockpicks, ink kit, two smoke tags, and a writ that will not survive a careful reader.
Sign here. Not with your real name, obviously."

nextObjectiveId.text: Take the kit.

objectives.description: Cross to the archive district under dark.

The safehouse smells of cold tea. Through the shutter slat you can see the archive door across the alley.

Two guards, one circuit, four minutes apart. There will be a service way in around the back, and a roof line if you would rather be quick than careful.

nextObjectiveId.text: Find the way in.

objectives.description: Work the alley behind the archive and map the ways in.

Three ways in, and the patrol turns in ninety seconds.

The coal chute is filthy, blind and slow. The roof line is quick and completely exposed. The front door would take the writ and a steady face.

nextObjectiveId.text: Take the coal chute. Slow and unseen.
Go over the roof line. Fast and loud.
Walk in with the writ.

objectives.description: Crawl the coal chute, one shoulder at a time, and drop into the cellar.

You come out under the stacks with soot in your teeth and nobody the wiser.

Above you the building is quiet in the way that means everyone in it believes they are alone.

nextObjectiveId.text: Get to the stacks.

objectives.description:
The tiles are wet and one of them moves under your foot.

Across the roof a lookout turns, sees you, and does not shout. He reaches for the bell rope instead, which is worse.

nextObjectiveId.text: Stop him.

objectives.description: Take the lookout down before he reaches the rope.
objectives.drawDescription: Neither side yielded. The contract stands.
objectives.failDescription: They were stronger than the posting suggested. Regroup.

objectives.description:
He does not reach it. But he got a hand to it, and somewhere below a small bell moved once.

One ring is not an alarm. It is a question. Someone in this building is already walking toward the answer.

nextObjectiveId.text: Get inside before they find it.

objectives.description:
The clerk reads the writ twice, which is once more than you wanted.

"Requisition, then. Which index do you need pulled?"

nextObjectiveId.text: The autumn index.
The index for the year, all of it.
Whichever one the Kage's office uses.

objectives.description:
He nods, bored, and writes it down. Everyone who works here knows they file by season. Only outsiders ask for a year.

"Third aisle, and do not take the lamp past the ledgers."
He goes back to his tea. You walk into the archive through the front door like a man with business here.

nextObjectiveId.text: Walk in.

objectives.description:
He smiles, and the smile does not reach anything.

"We do not index by year. Never have."
The writ goes in his pocket, not back in your hand, and two men walk you out. By the time you are in the alley again the lamps are lit on the upper floor and the building knows it has a visitor.

nextObjectiveId.text: Go over the roof, then. Nothing quiet left to lose.

objectives.description:
Rows of shelving run back into the dark, every one packed with rolled paper.

Somewhere below, a single lamp is still burning. Seasons, not years. The autumn shelves are the far wall.

nextObjectiveId.text: Search the autumn shelves.

objectives.description: Search the seasonal shelves for the transfer ledger.

The ledger is ordinary until the last three pages.

Every transfer in the same neat hand, buyer left, price right. Your village letters are listed twice.
The name beside them is one you have heard in a briefing room, on the other side of the table.

nextObjectiveId.text: Copy the page and get the files.

objectives.description: Work the seal on the file drawer.

Someone has been in the room the whole time.

He steps out from between the shelves without hurrying, which is worse than if he ran. No crest, no colours, nothing to say who pays him. Only the way he stands, which says he has done this before.
objectives.drawDescription: Neither side yielded. The contract stands.
objectives.failDescription: They were stronger than the posting suggested. Regroup.

objectives.description: Take the ledger and the files out the way you came, and cross back over the border before first light.

The Commander reads the page twice, then sets it face down on the map.

"You were not seen. Good.
As for this name, you will forget you read it until I tell you to remember. That is not a request, and it is not for your protection."

nextObjectiveId.text: Understood.

data.name: Witness Detail
data.description: An hour before dawn a witness has to reach a hearing on the other side of the village, and the people who want her absent were paid to take her alive. Three ways across. All of them end in a fight.
data.successDescription: She reached the steps and she gave the name.

objectives.description:
The handler does not sit down, and does not offer you tea. She lays a folded contract on the table and turns it so the price faces you.

"Somebody bought her. Not her death, her absence. Take, was the word they used."

nextObjectiveId.text: Absence buys silence. Death buys questions.
Explain it slowly.

objectives.description:
She does not agree out loud. She taps the table twice with one finger, the way you tap a wall in the dark to find the door.

"The last one I sent asked me why they had not simply killed her. Since you are quicker than him, keep up. The Unsigned chalk a lane before they work it, one stroke, low on the corner stone. Not a warning to you. A note they leave each other."

nextObjectiveId.text: Then I will read their notes.

objectives.description:
She looks up properly for the first time, and does not quite hide that she is reassessing you.

"Slowly, then. A body is a crime. Somebody has to investigate a crime, and investigating this one means reading the ledger she was going to talk about. A witness who simply fails to arrive is nobody's case at all. Now, the Unsigned chalk a lane before they work it. One stroke, low on the corner stone. It is not a warning meant for you, it is a note they leave each other."

nextObjectiveId.text: Then I will read their notes.

objectives.description:
Kanna is twenty two, has not slept, and holds a rolled statement against her chest like it is the only warm thing she owns.

"They came to my father's house first," she says. "They were very polite about it. That is the part I keep thinking about."

nextObjectiveId.text: Stay at my left shoulder.

objectives.description:
She is at the door with her coat already on, standing at your left shoulder like she was told. Past it the village is dark for another hour, and somewhere in that hour people are standing very still, waiting to be told which way the two of you went.

"You choose," she says. "I have been choosing all week and look where it put me."

nextObjectiveId.text: The market road. Loud rooms hide loud men.
The back lanes. Slow, blind, ours.
Give me your coat. You walk alone.

objectives.description: The market road is loud with carts before dawn, which is cover of a kind, and a hundred witnesses, which is not.

A fruit seller looks at you twice and then does not look at all. Two men come through the crowd at walking pace, because hurrying is what a crowd remembers.

"The polite one is on the left," Kanna says. Her voice does not shake, which is somehow worse.

nextObjectiveId.text: Put her behind me.

objectives.description: Two of them working the crowd. Neither one looks at Kanna, which means each is counting on the other to reach her first.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent
objectives.successDescription: The crowd closes over it before it has finished happening. She has not moved from behind your shoulder.

objectives.description: The back lanes take three times as long and cross no open ground at all. A patrol passes the lane mouth and you wait it out with her hand over her own mouth.

Chalk on the corner stone. One stroke, low down, unweathered. The rain stopped two hours ago.

"It is only chalk," Kanna whispers. "Children do that."

nextObjectiveId.text: Children do not chalk at midnight. Take the parallel.
Children, then. Walk it.

objectives.description:
You take the parallel and leave theirs empty. Somewhere behind you a lane that somebody spent the evening preparing stays quiet all the way to dawn, and nobody standing in it ever learns why.

"Children," Kanna says, eventually. "Yes. That was stupid of me."

nextObjectiveId.text: Keep moving.

objectives.description: Not children. The lane was chalked because it is long, and blind, and opens at one end, and what is waiting at that end has been waiting a while.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent
objectives.successDescription: You get out of the lane. It costs you.

objectives.description:
The coat is tight across your shoulders and smells of her house. She takes the servants' stair without being told twice.

"If they take you instead of me," she says from the dark, "I am still going. I wanted you to know that first."

nextObjectiveId.text: Good. Go.

objectives.description: They send the good one after the coat. She works out that it is empty about four steps too late, and does not stop, because she was not paid to stop.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent
objectives.successDescription: The coat is ruined. Kanna is three streets away and has not been touched.

objectives.description: The hearing hall stands at the top of eleven steps. The bell has not rung.

Someone has been sitting on the steps long enough that the frost has taken the shape of him. He stands at the exact distance where leaving stops being something you can do quietly.

"She has an hour," he says. "I only need her to miss it."

nextObjectiveId.text: Then you come through me first.

objectives.description: He takes you up on it without a word. No lane, no crowd, no coat. Eleven steps, and a bell about to ring.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent
objectives.successDescription: The bell rings on the second stroke of it. She walks up past you and does not look down.

objectives.description:
The clerk checks the hour before he checks her name, and writes them down in that order.

"If she had come in after the bell," he says, still writing, "I would have noted that instead, and there would be nothing here to hear. No crime in it. The record does not ask why a person was late."

nextObjectiveId.text: One hour. That was the whole price of her.

objectives.description: Witness delivered, statement taken.

You come to in a doorway with your collar gone stiff. Two doors down, behind the water butt, something that has been holding still for twenty minutes moves.

"I did what you told me," Kanna says. "The bell has not rung yet. Get up."

nextObjectiveId.text: Get up.

objectives.description: The safehouse, the lamp oil, the three ways across the village.
